examples.ko: 이 연구는 의학계에서 큰 관심을 받았어요.
examples.en: This study received great attention in the medical world.
The medical community evaluated the new treatment cautiously.

examples.ko: 의학계의 의견이 아직 하나로 모이지 않았어요.
examples.en: Opinion in the medical world has not yet come together.
He is a professor respected in the medical field.
New news reached the medical world.
People working in medicine gathered and held a discussion.

explain: '~계'는 어떤 분야에 있는 사람들 전체를 가리켜요. 정치계, 교육계, 학계처럼 쓰고, 의학계는 의사와 연구자 등 의학 분야 사람들을 두루 말해요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 치료법은 의학계의 관심을 끌고 있어요.
phrases.en: This treatment is attracting the attention of the medical community.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연구나 발견이 주목받을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when research or a discovery gets noticed.

phrases.en: That doctor is an expert recognized in the medical world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의학 분야 사람들에게 능력을 인정받는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being recognized by people in the medical field.

phrases.en: Medical experts gathered for the conference.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 의사나 연구자를 소개할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news to introduce doctors or researchers.

explain_en: '~계' refers to all the people in a certain field, as in 정치계, 교육계 and 학계. '의학계' broadly means the people in medicine, such as doctors and researchers. It appears often in the news.

examples.en: A healthy liver was transplanted into the patient.
The flowers in the pot are transplanted to the garden.

examples.ko: 이식된 피부가 잘 붙어서 의사가 안심했어요.
examples.en: The doctor was relieved because the transplanted skin took well.

examples.ko: 어린 나무는 봄에 이식되는 것이 좋아요.
examples.en: Young trees are best transplanted in spring.

examples.ko: 새 장기가 이식되면 몇 주 동안 병원에 있어야 해요.
examples.en: Once a new organ is transplanted, you have to stay in the hospital for a few weeks.

examples.ko: 이 게임 프로그램은 다른 기기로도 이식될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This game program can also be ported to other devices.

explain: 몸의 장기나 피부, 식물을 다른 곳으로 옮겨 심을 때 써요. 의료 뉴스에 특히 자주 나와요. 프로그램을 다른 기계에 맞게 옮기는 것도 같은 말로 해요. 하는 쪽은 '이식하다'예요.

phrases.en: He had a liver transplant operation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 장기를 옮기는 수술을 가리키는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase for an operation that transplants an organ.

phrases.en: A kidney was transplanted into the patient in yesterday's surgery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇이 옮겨졌는지 주어로 분명히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear what was transplanted by making it the subject.

phrases.en: A large tree was transplanted to the park in spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 몸이 아니라 식물을 다른 곳으로 옮겨 심을 때도 같은 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same word is also used when a plant, not a body part, is moved and replanted.

explain_en: Used when an organ, skin or plant is moved and planted somewhere else, and it appears a lot in medical news. Moving a program to another device is also described with this word. The active form is 이식하다.

examples.en: The flu spreads easily through coughs and sneezes.
This disease isn't passed on to humans.

examples.ko: 아이들이 모이는 곳에서는 병이 전염되는 속도가 빨라요.
examples.en: In places where children gather, illnesses spread faster.
They say yawns are contagious to the person next to you.
My coworker's anxiety rubbed off on me too.

examples.ko: 손을 씻으면 병이 전염될 가능성이 줄어요.
examples.en: Washing your hands lowers the chance of the illness spreading.

explain: 병이 사람에서 사람으로 옮을 때 써요. 일상에서는 같은 뜻으로 '옮다'를 많이 써서 '감기가 옮았어요'라고 해요. 하품이나 기분처럼 병이 아닌 것에도 비유로 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 병이 전염되지 않도록 손을 자주 씻어요.
phrases.en: I wash my hands often so the illness doesn't spread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 옮는 것을 막으려는 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses the purpose of preventing an illness from spreading.

phrases.en: The yawn was contagious, so I yawned too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 아닌 것이 다른 사람에게 번질 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for non-diseases that spread to other people.

phrases.en: I caught a cold from my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '전염되다' 대신 더 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler everyday word used more often than 전염되다.

explain_en: Disease passes from person to person (감기가 전염되다) It is used when a disease passes from one person to another. In daily talk people often say 옮다 for the same idea, as in '감기가 옮았어요' (I caught a cold from someone). It can also be used figuratively for yawns or moods.

t90.ax: This disease isn't passed on to humans.

examples.ko: 아이가 쩔뚝쩔뚝 걸어서 무슨 일인지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: The child was walking with a limp, so I asked what happened.

examples.ko: 다리를 다친 고양이가 쩔뚝쩔뚝 걸어 와요.
examples.en: The cat with the hurt leg is limping over.

examples.ko: 아버지는 무릎이 아파서 쩔뚝쩔뚝 계단을 올라가세요.
examples.en: My father's knee hurts, so he climbs the stairs with a limp.

examples.ko: 신발 한 짝이 벗겨져서 쩔뚝쩔뚝 뛰어갔어요.
examples.en: One shoe came off, so I ran off in a lopsided hobble.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 경기가 끝나고 쩔뚝쩔뚝 걸어 나왔어요.
examples.en: After the game, that player came out limping.

examples.ko: 왜 오늘은 쩔뚝쩔뚝 걸어요? 어디 아파요?
examples.en: Why are you limping today? Does something hurt?

explain: 다리가 불편해서 몸이 좌우로 기우뚱하며 걷는 모습을 그리는 말이에요. 뒤에 '걷다, 걸어가다' 같은 동사가 자주 와요.

phrases.en: That person walked off with a limp.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쩔뚝쩔뚝'과 같은 뜻이고 소리가 더 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '쩔뚝쩔뚝' with a softer sound.

phrases.en: My foot hurt, so I walked with a limp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아파서 몸이 기우뚱하며 걷는 모습을 말할 때 가장 기본으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for walking unevenly because of pain.

explain_en: It paints the picture of someone walking with the body tilting side to side because of a bad leg. Verbs like '걷다' and '걸어가다' often follow it.

examples.en: Given time, emotional wounds heal too.

examples.ko: 그 병은 약을 꾸준히 먹으면 치유될 수 있어요.
examples.en: That illness can be cured if you keep taking the medicine.

examples.ko: 여행을 다녀오니 지친 마음이 치유된 것 같아요.
examples.en: After the trip, I feel like my tired mind has healed.

examples.ko: 상처가 다 치유되어서 이제 아프지 않아요.
examples.en: The wound has fully healed, so it doesn't hurt anymore.

examples.ko: 숲을 걷다 보면 저절로 치유되는 기분이에요.
examples.en: Walking in the forest, I feel like I'm healing on my own.

examples.ko: 아픈 기억이 치유됐다고 말하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say their painful memories have healed.

explain: '치유되다'는 몸의 병보다 마음의 상처에 특히 많이 써요. 일상에서 병이 나을 때는 '낫다'가 더 쉽고 자연스러워요. '치료되다'는 병원에서 치료를 받아 좋아지는 것이고, '치유되다'는 시간이나 환경 덕분에 저절로 회복되는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 노래를 들으면 마음이 치유되는 것 같아요.
phrases.en: When I hear that song, I feel my heart healing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음, 상처와 가장 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs best with heart and emotional wounds.

phrases.example: 이 병은 일찍 발견하면 치료될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This illness can be cured if found early.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 병이 좋아질 때는 '치료되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 치료되다 when an illness is cured through medical care.

phrases.en: My cold got better in a few days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 좋아질 때 일상에서 가장 쉽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easiest everyday word for recovering from illness.

explain_en: Wounds heal, also emotionally, with a gentler feel. 치유되다 is used even more for emotional wounds than for physical illness. In everyday talk about an illness getting better, 낫다 is easier and more natural. 치료되다 means getting better through medical treatment, while 치유되다 feels like recovering naturally through time or surroundings.

dis.h: healed, also emotionally or from wounds
gh: an illness is cured by medical care

p.n: 치료되다 sounds clinical; less natural for the heart.

t90.ax: Given time, emotional wounds heal too.

examples.ko: 암 환자들이 호스피스 병동에서 편안하게 지내요.
examples.en: Cancer patients stay comfortably in the hospice ward.
My mother spent her final days in a hospice.
I applied for hospice volunteer work.
Hospice care focuses on comfort rather than treatment.
The family is looking into hospice hospitals.
A hospice nurse takes care of the patient and the family.

explain: 일반 병원이 병을 고치는 데 목표를 두는 것과 달리, 통증을 줄이고 환자와 가족의 마음을 돌보는 데 중심을 둬요. 법과 뉴스에서는 '호스피스·완화의료'를 함께 말하는 경우가 많아요. 장소를 말할 때는 '호스피스 병동'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 할머니는 집 근처 호스피스 병원에 계세요.
phrases.en: My grandmother is at a hospice hospital near home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이나 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the facility.

phrases.en: I did hospice volunteer work in college.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자를 돕는 봉사 활동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for volunteer work helping patients.

phrases.en: I looked up how to apply for hospice and palliative care.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 법에서 함께 묶어 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair often used together in news and law.

explain_en: Unlike a regular hospital that aims to cure illness, it focuses on easing pain and caring for the patient and family emotionally. In law and news, 'hospice and palliative care' (호스피스·완화의료) are often mentioned together. For the place, people say '호스피스 병동'.

en: to be sucked; to be inhaled

examples.en: Dust is sucked into the vacuum cleaner.
It is dangerous if smoke is inhaled into the body.
Air is being drawn in through this hole.

examples.ko: 흡입된 가루가 폐에 쌓일 수 있어요.
examples.en: The inhaled powder can build up in the lungs.
There was an accident where clothing got sucked into a machine.

examples.ko: 독한 가스가 흡입되지 않게 마스크를 쓰세요.
examples.en: Wear a mask so that toxic gas isn't inhaled.

explain: 공기, 연기, 먼지 같은 것이 몸이나 기계 안으로 빨려 들어올 때 써요. '들이마시다'는 사람이 하는 행동이고, '흡입되다'는 그 결과를 설명하는 말이라 의학이나 안전 안내문에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Fine dust gets inhaled through the nose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸 어디로 들어오는지 '코로', '입으로'처럼 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can say where it enters the body, such as 코로 or 입으로.

phrases.en: I open the window so the gas is not inhaled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해로운 것이 몸에 들어오지 않게 조심할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when being careful so that something harmful doesn't get in.

phrases.en: Dust gets sucked into the vacuum cleaner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흡입되다'를 쉬운 말로 바꾼 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler way to say 흡입되다.

explain_en: To be drawn in — passive, technical, air or smoke taken in (흡입되다) It describes air, smoke, or dust being drawn into a body or machine. 들이마시다 is what a person does, whereas 흡입되다 describes the result and appears often in medical or safety notices.

en: to be opened to the public (museum, library)

examples.en: The new art museum opens next week.
This library was opened in 1998.

examples.ko: 박물관이 개관된 지 벌써 십 년이 지났어요.
examples.en: It has already been ten years since the museum opened.
The science museum for citizens has finally opened.

examples.ko: 개관되기 전에 직원들이 청소를 열심히 했어요.
examples.en: Before the opening, the staff cleaned hard.
When is this exhibition hall scheduled to open?

explain: 개관되다는 도서관·박물관·미술관·전시관처럼 '관'이 붙은 곳이 문을 열 때만 써요. 가게나 식당은 '개업하다', '오픈하다'라고 해요. 문을 여는 사람이 주어이면 '개관하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 새 박물관은 다음 달 개관 예정이에요.
phrases.en: The new museum is scheduled to open next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 열 날짜를 안내할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in announcements about the opening date.

phrases.en: As soon as the art museum opened, many people came.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 열 곳이 주어일 때 '개관되다'를 쓰고, 문을 연 바로 그때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 개관되다 when the place that opens is the subject; this phrase means right at the moment of opening.

phrases.en: The new art museum opened yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '문을 열다'가 더 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, 문을 열다 is easier and more common.

explain_en: Museum or library opens for the first time (도서관이 개관되다) 개관되다 is only for places whose names end in 관, such as a library, museum or exhibition hall. Shops and restaurants use 개업하다 or 오픈하다 instead. If the person opening it is the subject, use 개관하다.

dis.h: a museum or library is opened
gh: open a venue to the public
a school is founded and opens

p.n: 개장 is for outdoor places like beaches or markets, not libraries.

examples.en: The illegally parked car was towed.
My car broke down, so I called a tow.
The towing fee was more expensive than I expected.
A tow truck came and took the car away.
Towing is covered by insurance, so it is free.
A towing operation is going on on the road.

explain: 주로 차에 쓰는 말이라 '견인차', '견인료', '견인되다'로 많이 써요. 고장 났을 때는 '견인을 부르다', 불법 주차로 끌려갔을 때는 '견인당하다'라고 해요. '끌다'는 일상 말이고, 견인은 차를 끌고 가는 일에 쓰는 전문적인 말이에요.

phrases.example: 견인차가 와서 고장 난 차를 끌고 갔어요.
phrases.en: A tow truck came and took the broken-down car away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 끌고 가는 차를 말해요. 길에서 사고가 났을 때 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: The truck that tows cars; called when there is trouble on the road.

phrases.en: The towing fee was fifty thousand won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 끌고 간 값을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The fee charged for towing a vehicle.

phrases.example: 제 차가 어제 견인돼서 찾으러 갔어요.
phrases.en: My car was towed yesterday, so I went to pick it up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 주어로 해서 끌려갔다는 말이에요. 불법 주차 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the car as the subject, meaning it was towed; common in talk about illegal parking.

explain_en: It is mostly used for cars: '견인차' (tow truck), '견인료' (towing fee), '견인되다' (get towed). After a breakdown you '견인을 부르다'; when towed for illegal parking you say '견인당하다'. '끌다' is the everyday word; 견인 is the technical term for towing a vehicle.

examples.en: The hull of the ship hit a rock and got scratched.
Water slowly came into the hull.
Large ships have their hulls made of steel.

examples.ko: 선체 길이가 삼백 미터나 되는 배예요.
examples.en: It is a ship with a hull three hundred meters long.

examples.ko: 수리 중이라서 선체에 페인트를 새로 칠했어요.
examples.en: It is under repair, so they repainted the hull.
Divers are inspecting the sunken hull.

explain: 배의 몸통 부분만 가리켜요. 배 전체는 '배'라고 하고, 큰 배를 격식 있게 부를 때는 '선박'이라고 해요. 사고 뉴스에서 '선체 인양'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Raising the hull began after the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가라앉은 배를 물 위로 끌어올릴 때 뉴스에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news for lifting a sunken ship out of the water.

phrases.en: The hull tilted because of the strong wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배의 몸통이 한쪽으로 기운 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the ship's body leaning to one side.

phrases.en: The damage to the hull was not big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고 뒤 배 몸통의 피해를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for damage to the ship's body after an accident.

explain_en: Hull of a ship; shipbuilding, maritime. It points only to the body of a ship. The whole vessel is 배, and 선박 is the formal word for a large ship. It often appears in accident news, as in 선체 인양 (raising the hull).

examples.ko: 그 사람은 경찰서 유치장에서 하룻밤을 보냈대요.
examples.en: I heard that person spent one night in the police station's holding cell.

examples.ko: 영화에서 주인공이 유치장에 갇히는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: There's a scene in the movie where the main character is locked in a holding cell.
The police took the man to the holding cell.
I heard it's cold and dark inside a holding cell.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 유치장 환경이 좋지 않다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The news said the conditions in holding cells are poor.

examples.ko: 하룻밤 유치장 신세를 졌다고 친구가 웃으며 말했어요.
examples.en: My friend said with a laugh that he spent a night in a holding cell.

explain: 경찰서 안에서 사람을 잠시 가두는 곳이에요. 재판을 받고 형이 정해진 사람이 지내는 '교도소'와는 달라서 둘을 구별해서 써야 해요. '유치장에 갇히다/넣다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 술에 취해 싸운 사람이 밤새 유치장에 갇혔어요.
phrases.en: The man who got into a drunken fight was held in a cell overnight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본인이 그곳에 가둬지는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is locked up there.
phrases.en_equiv: to be locked in a holding cell

phrases.en: The police put that person in a holding cell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 가두는 쪽의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of those who detain the person.
phrases.en_equiv: to put in a holding cell

phrases.example: 그는 다음 날 아침에 유치장에서 나왔어요.
phrases.en: He came out of the holding cell the next morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀려나서 밖으로 나오는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes being released and coming out.
phrases.en_equiv: to get out of a holding cell

explain_en: It is a place inside a police station where a person is held for a short time. It differs from '교도소' (prison), where people serve a sentence after trial, so keep the two apart. It is used as '유치장에 갇히다/넣다'.

t90.ax: The police took the man to the holding cell.

examples.en: The raising of the sunken ship has begun.
The salvage work took a month.
The salvage was postponed because of bad weather.
The salvage succeeded, and the families shed tears.
The raising of the ship and the investigation proceed separately.

examples.ko: 오랜 인양 끝에 유물이 바다 위로 올라왔어요.
examples.en: After a long salvage, the relics came up from the sea.

explain: '인양'은 물에 가라앉은 배, 차, 유물을 끌어올리는 일에 써요. 사람이나 작은 물건을 건질 때는 '건지다', '구조하다'를 써요. 뉴스에서 '선박 인양', '인양 작업'으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Raising a ship costs a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인양'과 가장 자주 함께 나오는 말로, 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word most often paired with 인양, common in news.

phrases.en: They finally succeeded in raising the sunken ship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끌어올리는 일이 잘 끝났다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the raising work ended well.

phrases.en: The sunken ship was raised yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끌어올려지는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of what is being raised.

explain_en: '인양' is for raising sunken ships, cars or relics out of the water. For rescuing people or fishing out small things, use '건지다' or '구조하다'. In the news you often see '선박 인양' and '인양 작업'.

en: to sink; to collapse; to cave in

examples.ko: 도로가 갑자기 함몰돼서 차가 지나가지 못해요.
examples.en: The road suddenly caved in, so cars can't get through.
The ground may cave in, so please be careful.
The building's floor caved in because of the earthquake.

examples.ko: 빗물 때문에 지반이 함몰되는 일이 가끔 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes the ground sinks because of rainwater.

examples.ko: 사고로 차 앞부분이 안쪽으로 함몰된 채 서 있었어요.
examples.en: The car stood there with its front caved inward from the accident.

examples.ko: 볼이 푹 함몰되어 보일 만큼 살이 빠졌어요.
examples.en: I lost so much weight that my cheeks look sunken.

explain: 땅, 도로, 건물 바닥처럼 표면이 안쪽으로 푹 꺼질 때 써요. 일상에서는 '꺼지다', '푹 들어가다'가 더 자연스럽고, '함몰되다'는 뉴스나 설명하는 글에서 많이 나와요. 주어가 스스로 꺼지는 말이라 목적어는 없어요.

phrases.en: Construction has started to repair the sunken road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '함몰되다'의 과거형 '함몰된'으로 이미 꺼진 곳을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form '함몰된' describes a place that has already sunk.

phrases.example: 공사를 해서 땅이 함몰되지 않도록 했어요.
phrases.en: They did construction so the ground would not cave in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 '꺼지지 않게 막다'라는 안전 이야기에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is often used in safety talk about preventing a collapse.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 와서 바닥이 푹 꺼졌어요.
phrases.en: It rained a lot, so the floor sank in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '함몰되다'보다 일상적이고 쉬운 말이라 대화에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a simpler, everyday way to say it in conversation.

explain_en: Formal, written; ground or surface caves in (땅이 함몰되다) Use it when a surface such as ground, a road or a floor sinks inward. In daily talk '꺼지다' or '푹 들어가다' sounds more natural, while '함몰되다' appears in news and explanatory writing. It takes no object because the subject sinks by itself.

t90.ax: The ground may cave in, so please be careful.

en: to be severed; to come to a rupture

examples.en: Because of heavy snow, traffic to the village was cut off.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 연락이 몇 년 동안 단절되었어요.
examples.en: Contact between the two was cut off for several years.

examples.ko: 인터넷이 단절되면 일을 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: If the internet is cut off, I can't work.

examples.ko: 가족과 단절된 채로 혼자 살아가는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people live alone, cut off from their families.

examples.ko: 다툰 뒤에 친구와의 관계가 완전히 단절되고 말았어요.
examples.en: After the fight, my relationship with my friend was completely severed.

examples.ko: 전기 공급이 단절될까 봐 미리 손전등을 준비했어요.
examples.en: I prepared a flashlight in advance in case the power supply got cut off.

explain: 단절되다는 교통·통신·연락·관계처럼 이어져 있던 것이 끊길 때 써요. '끊어지다'가 더 일상적이고, '단절되다'는 완전히 끊겨 다시 잇기 어려운 느낌이 있어요. 줄이나 실처럼 눈에 보이는 물건에는 '끊어지다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 크게 싸운 뒤 친구와 관계가 단절됐어요.
phrases.en: After a big fight, my relationship with my friend was cut off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 사이의 관계가 완전히 끊길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a relationship between people is completely cut off.

phrases.en: When communication breaks down in a family, people feel lonely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 말이 오가지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when communication stops between people.

phrases.en: The phone call suddenly got cut off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '끊어지다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, 끊어지다 is more natural.

explain_en: 단절되다 is for things that were connected and then break off, such as traffic, communication, contact or a relationship. 끊어지다 is the everyday word; 단절되다 feels more complete and hard to restore. For visible things like a rope or thread, use 끊어지다.

en: to disgrace oneself; to make an exhibition of oneself

examples.en: I was greatly humiliated in front of everyone.
I got embarrassed at the interview because I got the name wrong.
If you do that, you will lose face.
I was shamed in front of my friends, and my face turned red.
I prepared hard so I wouldn't be humiliated.

examples.ko: 시험에서 꼴찌를 해서 망신당할까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm afraid I'll be humiliated by coming in last on the test.

explain: '망신당하다'는 다른 사람들 앞에서 실수하거나 잘못이 드러나서 체면을 잃는 거예요. 내 잘못이든 아니든 남이 보는 곳에서 창피한 일을 겪는다는 느낌이에요. '창피하다'는 부끄러운 마음 자체이고, 망신당하다는 그런 일을 겪는 상황이에요.

phrases.en: I was disgraced in front of my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '망신당하다'를 띄어 쓴 모양이에요. 뜻은 같고 '망신'을 조금 더 또렷하게 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced-out version of '망신당하다' with the same meaning, putting a little more emphasis on '망신'.

phrases.example: 발표 때 망신당하지 않으려고 많이 연습했어요.
phrases.en: I practiced a lot so I wouldn't embarrass myself in the presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 창피한 일을 피하고 싶다는 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the goal of avoiding a humiliating situation.
phrases.en_equiv: so as not to be disgraced

phrases.en: I'm worried I'll be humiliated in front of people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안 좋은 일이 생길까 걱정하는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express worry that something bad might happen.

explain_en: 망신당하다 means losing face when a mistake or fault is exposed in front of others. 창피하다 is the feeling of embarrassment itself, while 망신당하다 is the situation of going through it publicly.
